Proactive Assistant Training Databenchmarks · open models · annotation samples · as of 16 Sep 2026

Literature review for a proactive streaming visual assistant · compiled 16 Sep 2026

What to benchmark on, who leads, and how their training data was made

This page answers three questions. (1) Are there good benchmarks newer than Ego-MC-Bench, Pro2Bench and OmniAssistBench? (2) Which models lead those benchmarks? (3) For the open models that do well, what data were they trained on, how was it annotated, and how big are they? The training-data viewer (second tab) shows real released training records on a timeline next to the video, where the license allows.

Short answer.

(1) Yes, several newer benchmarks exist. None clearly supersedes your three. The most useful new ones are ProactiveBench (Sep, the strictest per-second when-to-speak protocol, not yet released), StreamArena (Aug, human-annotated hour-long streams), VIABench (Jul, real footage from blind users) and GuideMe (Jul, large, but its dialogue is written by an LLM).

(2) No open model leads everywhere. The winners on the task-guidance benchmarks are small models fine-tuned by the benchmark authors on their own data: Qwen3.5-2B on Ego-MC-Bench, and Qwen3.6-VL-27B and Llama-4-Maverick on Pro2Bench. On the omni benchmarks the best open models are Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B and MiniCPM-o 4.5, neither trained on any disclosed proactive data.

(3) In every released training set, the timing labels (when the assistant speaks) are derived: from step boundaries, caption windows, ASR timestamps or an LLM's pick. None records when a real helper chose to speak. The only human-timed sets are QICD (213 videos, feedback always after the error) and the Ego-MC-Bench test set.

1 · Terms and the scores behind the leaderboards

A proactive streaming assistant watches a live video (sometimes audio too) and decides, moment by moment, whether to speak. Each benchmark turns that into one of three evaluation shapes:

Evaluation shapeWhat the model doesBenchmarks
True streamingFrames arrive in time order; at every tick (1 s, a frame, or a unit) the model speaks or stays silent. Speaking early, late or never are all errors.ProactiveBench, OmniInteract, Omni-DuplexEval, VideoFDB, Ego-MC-Bench (fine-tuned models)
Interval classificationThe benchmark gives fixed clips (e.g. 8 s); for each clip the model says $interrupt$ + text or $silent$.Pro2Bench / EgoProactive challenge, GuideMe (anchor mode)
Timestamp QAA question is asked at a fixed time about the video so far, and the model answers once; there is no speak/silent decision.OmniAssistBench (with a "[KEEP QUIET]" option), S-EMBER, StreamArena (reactive part)

The headline metrics, written out:

Ego-MC-Bench mistake F1 = 2PR/(P+R); a prediction matches a ground-truth feedback within a 30 s window Pro2Bench G-Mean F1 = √( F1_interrupt · F1_silent ) PQS = mean over decisions of { 1 if correct silence ; g∈[0,1] (GPT-5.2 judge) if correct interrupt ; 0 otherwise } EgoProactive challenge macro-F1 = ½ ( F1_interrupt + F1_silent ) (text is not scored) ProactiveBench AVG = mean of 6 subtask scores; window tasks score the FIRST non-silent second (early / in-window / missed) OmniAssistBench = GPT-5 judge, 0–5 per turn → 0–100 (accuracy, completeness, whether it correctly stayed quiet)

G-Mean F1 punishes a model that always talks or never talks: one factor goes to zero. Macro-F1 does not. An always-silent policy already scores about 1/3, which helps explain why a 0-parameter GRU cadence model scored 0.608 in the challenge against the winner's 0.718.

2 · The three benchmarks you named

"Pro2Bench" appears only as a section title inside Meta's paper Plan, Watch, Recover (arXiv 2606.04970), which is why searching for the name finds nothing. Its real-glasses split, EgoProactive, is the data for the ECCV 2026 Wearable AI Challenge and the facebook/wearable-ai dataset behind the wearable-ai viewer you linked.

From May 2026, just before your window: OmniInteract (2605.26485, good, self-recorded with spoken queries, run through each model's native real-time API; MiniCPM-o 4.5 0.368 > AURA 0.363 > Gemini 2.5 Flash Live 0.344), Omni-DuplexEval (human duplex baseline 81.8 vs MiniCPM-o 4.5 39.6; co-authored by MiniCPM-o's developer) and VideoFDB (NVIDIA; nonverbal video-call dynamics, not task help). Weak or narrow: EgoPro-Bench, StreamPro-Bench, RealStreamEval, SOVBench, Streaming-Eval, OmniStarPro, SPRINT, MedStreamBench, StreamMemBench, PuzzleMate, OVIBench, Stream3D-Bench.

Interpretation. None of the new benchmarks combines what Ego-MC-Bench has (real helpers speaking at natural times, with mistakes) with scale. For a mistake-correcting assistant, the practical suite remains Ego-MC-Bench (gold timing) + EgoProactive / Pro2Bench (scale and planted mistakes). Add ProactiveBench once it is released, for strict silence discipline, and OmniInteract if audio matters.

The pattern: a small model fine-tuned with a speak/silent head on in-domain data beats zero-shot frontier models, but only on its authors' own benchmark. Nobody has evaluated one model across all three of your benchmarks. The fine-tunes that won Ego-MC-Bench and Pro2Bench are not released, so what you can reuse from them is their data recipe, below.

6 · The labelling recipes, compared

Across all of these sets, when-to-speak labels come from one of six recipes. The recipe determines what a model can learn from the data.

RecipeHow the speak time is setUsed byWhat it teaches, and the risk
A · Real helper, liveTimestamp of a real instructor's speechEgo-MC-Bench (test only), QICD (human-annotated after the fact)Natural timing, including anticipatory warnings. Tiny: ≈260 videos total.
B · Counterfactual rewriteLLM picks the first caption window where a made-up deviation "becomes visible"Ego-CoMist, LiveMamba's noun/verb swapsScales mistakes cheaply (25k). The video never shows an error, so the model learns instruction-vs-video mismatch, not visible mistakes. Times snap to 5 s.
C · Step-boundary ruleSpeak at step start or end (or mistake onset) from existing step labelsPro2Bench/PWR, GuideMe, ProAssist, MMDuet2 (Ego-Exo4D), JoyAI guided sessionsReliable and plentiful, but teaches cadence: the challenge's 0-parameter GRU reached 0.608 on timing priors alone.
D · VLM or agent labellerAn LLM/VLM watches the video and decides the momentsAmbient, JoyAI alerts, AURA, ROMA (re-timing), Gander (re-timing)Works on unlabelled video, at ≈$0.05 per clip. It can see the future, and its label errors are unmeasured (no set reports agreement with humans).
E · Speech-aligned commentaryASR word timestamps from real live commentaryLiveCC / Live-WhisperX, Proact-VLReal human timing at millions of clips, but for narration, not intervention.
F · Scripted duplex dialogueAn LLM writes the dialogue, and a timeline with onsets and overlaps is laid out; TTS voices itGander, MiniCPM-o, Baichuan-Omni, LongCatTeaches turn-taking, barge-in and backchannels; nothing about visual task state.

What follows for your own data. Every public set that has mistakes either invents them in text (B) or plants them in scripts (EgoProactive). Every large set times speech by rule or by an LLM (C, D). No released set records when a helper chose to speak about a mistake at scale; the closest are QICD (post-error only) and the 40-session Ego-MC-Bench test set. That gap is exactly what a simulator with forced errors and a graded helper can fill.

7 · Caveats

  • Several papers contradict themselves on counts: Pro2Bench (42,275 vs 40,008 eval items; 249,584 vs 314,290 train rows), JoyAI (4M+ claimed vs 3.02M released), Ego-CoMist (124 h vs 127.5 h computed). The viewer's stats files are computed from the released files.
  • Pro2Bench's human-correction and agreement figures are blank placeholders in the posted paper, so its human-check claims cannot be quantified.
  • Most leaderboards have no confidence intervals. ProactiveBench's top three are within 0.34 points.
  • Ego-CoMist and QICD annotations are under Qualcomm's no-redistribution research license. Keep this page private.
  • Citation counts were not collected (Semantic Scholar was rate-limited). GitHub stars and HF downloads are as of 16 Sep 2026.
